results.explanation: Grounding: the report's numbers trace to tool results. These include 152 events, all PEGGED; parents B and S; cancel_symmetry 0.9888; OTR 23 vs typical 25; cancel_ratio 0.96; size vs depth 1.02; price_move -1, post-cancel -0.5, reversion 0; six fills summing to 1914 (203+280+743+109+144+435); avg spread 2.53. Nothing is invented. Consistency: CLOSE_FP rests on one supported explanation (pegged two-parent algo, symmetric cancels at the touch, size equal to typical size). It also shows no benefit (adverse -1 tick move, no reversion), which matches the closure standard. Weaknesses: (1) Clarity: the sequence is not set out. No fill times (16:42:11.812, 15.414, 20.552 etc.) and no buy-cancel times are given, so a reviewer must rebuild the rest-fill-cancel order from the tape. E4 also says the fills were on 'the sell child' when they fell on several sell children. (2) Indicator vocabulary: listing 'opposite-side execution before the cancel' as not matched is wrong. Sell fills did occur while 2540 buy orders were resting, and those buys were then cancelled, which is the detector trigger. The report should say this feature is present but harmless, not absent. (3) The supported algo explanation has an empty ruled_out_by and cites no evidence IDs, though E1 and E2 support it. Genuine/partial execution is not discussed, although same_side_fill is 0. The closing message also says a first submission was rejected, but no such call appears in the conversation. Disposition and grounding are sound, but two or more points are weak.
results.label: Adequate
